nodes.name: graph_schema.py
nodes.summary: The project-agnostic schema half of the graph substrate: the controlled node_type and evidence_strength vocabularies, the pure lookup from evidence strength to a validation status, the required-core versus additive-optional front-matter split, and fail-closed validation that names the offending node. Carries no folder names, call, or partner nouns.
nodes.languageNotes: Vocabularies are frozensets and the evidence-to-status map is a plain dict lookup, never a judgement — that purity is what lets provenance be carried end to end. The newer tier/phase/artifact_path/sub_section_id keys are additive-optional so existing nodes still validate unchanged.

nodes.name: GraphSchemaError
nodes.summary: Raised on a front-matter violation, always naming the offending node reference.

nodes.name: map_evidence_to_status
nodes.summary: Maps an evidence_strength value to its constitutional validation status by pure dict lookup — source-grounded to confirmed, synthesis and inference to inferred, unconfirmed to unresolved — and is the single authority every graph tool reads that mapping from.

nodes.name: validate_front_matter
nodes.summary: Validates a node's front-matter against the schema: the required identity and provenance core must be present and non-blank, every controlled-vocabulary value must be in range, and any violation raises a named error rather than a silent default.

nodes.name: vault_reader.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic pure-Python parse layer of the graph substrate: reads every vault note's YAML front-matter, body prose, and wikilinks, validates each against the generic schema, and returns an indexed Vault. This is the single substrate the compiler, projector, pack deriver, and auditors all build on.
nodes.languageNotes: Wikilink resolution mirrors Obsidian's basename semantics, so [[Target]], [[Target|Display]] and [[folder/Target#Heading]] all land on the same node. A dangling link is recorded as a graph-quality signal rather than raised, while a duplicate id or basename fails closed.

nodes.name: VaultReadError
nodes.summary: Raised when a node has missing or malformed front-matter, an unparseable YAML block, a duplicate id or basename, or a schema violation — always naming the node.

nodes.name: WikiLink
nodes.summary: One parsed wikilink: its target basename plus the optional display text and heading anchor.

nodes.name: GraphNode
nodes.summary: One parsed vault node: its id, path, validated front-matter, body prose, outbound wikilinks, and mapped status, with accessors for the additive-optional tier, phase, artifact_path, and sub_section_id keys.

nodes.name: Vault
nodes.summary: The indexed parse result: path-ordered nodes plus id and basename indices, with methods to resolve a wikilink, find the config binding for a node, and enumerate dangling links.

nodes.name: _parse_wikilink
nodes.summary: Parses the inside of a wikilink into target, display text, and heading, handling the folder-prefixed and aliased forms.

nodes.name: _extract_wikilinks
nodes.summary: Scans a node body for wikilinks and returns them de-duplicated in first-seen order, keeping the parse deterministic.

nodes.name: _split_front_matter
nodes.summary: Splits a note into its YAML front-matter block and body, failing closed with the node reference when the block is missing or unparseable.

nodes.name: _parse_node
nodes.summary: Parses one note file into a GraphNode: splits the front-matter, validates it against the schema, extracts wikilinks, and computes the node's status from its evidence_strength.

nodes.name: read_vault
nodes.summary: Reads a whole vault directory into an indexed Vault: parses every note in sorted path order, builds the id and basename indices, and rejects duplicate ids or basenames.

nodes.name: vault_scaffold.py
nodes.summary: Instantiates a fresh per-project graph vault by copying the generic template — schema superset, folder skeleton, and a noun-free config — and rewriting a single project_id line, then validates the result by reading it back through the reader. Pure and Claude-free: a scaffolded vault holds no project facts until a human authors nodes into it.
nodes.languageNotes: The project_id swap is a single targeted regex substitution so the template config's explanatory comments survive the copy.

nodes.name: VaultScaffoldError
nodes.summary: Raised when a vault cannot be scaffolded — a bad template, a target collision, or a config with no project_id line to rewrite.

nodes.name: ScaffoldResult
nodes.summary: The outcome of scaffolding: the written vault root, the written config path, and the node root the reader and compiler will read.

nodes.name: scaffold_vault
nodes.summary: Copies the generic template to the target directory, rewrites the config's project_id, and returns the resolved vault, config, and node roots — refusing an existing target unless forced.

nodes.name: validate_scaffold
nodes.summary: Validates a scaffold by loading its config and reading the vault back through the reader, proving the new vault is one the compiler will accept.
